links.outcome: Readability grade level of LLM-generated caregiver education materials
links.effect: Mean FKGL ranged from 7.30 (DeepSeek-V3) to 9.41 (Copilot) and SMOG from 9.83 to 11.67, exceeding the recommended sixth-grade level despite prompts requesting simple language.
links.quote: Although readability levels were close to the average reading level of US adults (eighth grade) [ 36 ], they still exceeded American Medical Association recommendations (no more than sixth grade) for health education materials [ 37 ].

links.outcome: Whether LLM outputs provided source citations
links.effect: Only 1 of 4 models (Copilot) provided source citations. The other 3 gave answers without traceable sources.
links.quote: Only Copilot provides source citations, which raises concerns about the traceability and reliability of the information.

links.outcome: eHealth literacy and DDH knowledge after structured LLM training vs web search
links.effect: eHEALS group difference 1.73 (0.49-2.97) at T1 and 2.40 (1.13-3.67) at T2. DDH knowledge d=0.71 at T1 and 0.54 at T2. The group×time interaction was nonsignificant (P=.26).
links.quote: The intervention group showed higher scores than the control group at T1 (33.62, 95% CI 32.76-34.49; d =0.20, 95% CI 0.13-0.56) and T2 (33.27, 95% CI 32.38-34.17; d =0.36, 95% CI 0.01-0.80), indicating sustained improvements following the LLM-generated learning intervention.

links.outcome: Reading grade level of generated caregiver education materials
links.effect: Mean FKGL: DeepSeek-V3 7.30, Gemini 2.0 Flash 7.37, ChatGPT-4 8.74, and Copilot 9.41; all exceeded the recommended sixth-grade reading level despite simplified-language prompts.
links.quote: DeepSeek-V3 (mean 7.30, SD 1.08) and Gemini 2.0 Flash (mean 7.37, SD 1.33) produced sentences with superior FKGL scores compared to ChatGPT-4 (mean 8.74, SD 1.37) and Copilot (mean 9.41, SD 1.86).

links.outcome: Presence of source citations supporting generated educational information
links.effect: Only Copilot provided source citations among the four evaluated models.

links.outcome: Expert-rated accuracy of generated DDH education against clinical guidelines
links.effect: Responses rated “good” or “excellent” for accuracy: ChatGPT-4 85%, DeepSeek-V3 83%, Gemini 2.0 Flash 70%, and Copilot 66%; omissions were also reported for Copilot.
links.quote: In terms of accuracy, the proportion of “good” and “excellent” responses reached 85% for ChatGPT-4 and 83% for DeepSeek-V3, while Gemini 2.0 Flash (70%) and Copilot (66%) displayed a lower proportion.

links.effect: Significant differences found in accuracy, richness, fluency, understandability, and DISCERN scores among the 4 evaluated LLMs.
links.quote: There were significant differences between the 4 LLMs concerning accuracy, richness, fluency, Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool for Printable Materials Understandability, and DISCERN (P<.05).

links.effect: Structured AI literacy training for caregivers improved their eHealth literacy and DDH knowledge compared to a web search control.

links.effect: LLM-generated materials exceeded the 6th grade reading level recommendation for health education, documenting the hazard of inaccessible reading levels.
